text: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
Rescue me, LORD, from evil men; protect me from the violent,
who plot evil in their hearts and stir up war every day.
They sharpen their tongues like a serpent; the venom of a viper is under their lips. Selah
Guard me, LORD, from the hands of the wicked; protect me from the violent, who plot to trip up my feet.
The arrogant have hidden a trap for me; with cords they have spread a net beside the path and set snares for me. Selah

versions.text: The arrogant have hidden a trap for me; they have spread out cords into a net beside the path and set snares for me. Selah
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has 'with cords they spread a net' — the cords are the means, not the material being formed 'into a net.' The revised wording is both more accurate and smoother for reading aloud.

text: I say to the LORD: You are my God. Listen, LORD, to my cry for mercy.
LORD God, my mighty savior, you shield my head on the day of battle.
Do not grant the wicked their desires, LORD; do not let their schemes succeed, or they will exalt themselves. Selah
As for the head of those who surround me—let the malice of their own lips cover them.

versions.text: As for those who surround me—let the mischief of their own lips cover their heads.
versions.explanation: In the Hebrew, 'head' belongs to the first clause ('the head of those who surround me'), and the verb is 'cover them,' not 'cover their heads.' The suggested rendering keeps both elements in their proper places while remaining natural for oral reading.

versions.text: As for the heads of those who surround me—let the trouble their own lips cause cover them.
versions.explanation: The relative clause "the trouble their own lips cause cover them" stacks two verbs ("cause cover") back to back, which stumbles badly when read aloud. A simple noun phrase ("the malice of their own lips") renders עֲמַל שְׂפָתֵימוֹ just as accurately and flows cleanly. Hebrew רֹאשׁ is also singular here, so "the head" better matches the source while keeping the collective sense.

text: Let burning coals rain down on them; let them be thrown into the fire, into watery pits, never to rise again.
Let the slanderer find no footing in the land; let disaster hunt down the man of violence.
I know that the LORD secures justice for the poor and upholds the cause of the needy.
Surely the righteous will praise your name, and the upright will dwell in your presence.
